summary: The main gap is that the proposed closed-set prompt cannot be used through the unchanged `identify_strips` API. The review also focuses on the raw Converse payload contract, client lifecycle/credential reuse, exact perception parity, and source-pixel output integrity.

suggestions.title: Resolve the closed-set prompt injection contradiction
suggestions.rationale: `identify_strips` calls `build_identify_prompt` directly through `_run_call` and exposes no prompt-builder hook. A local `build_nova_identify_prompt` would be unused unless the example reimplements internals or monkeypatches production code. Either ship the shared open-set prompt for this baseline, or explicitly allow a narrow prompt-builder extension.

suggestions.title: Specify how the shim consumes structured_output
suggestions.rationale: `VisionAdapter` passes a Pydantic class as `structured_output`, while raw Bedrock `converse` receives fields such as `modelId`, `messages`, `inferenceConfig`, and `system`; it does not accept the adapter's provider-neutral keyword. The shim must consume the schema, add a JSON-schema instruction or equivalent prompt contract, call Converse, and return text for `VisionAdapter._extract` to validate. Passing the Pydantic class through to AWS will fail.

suggestions.title: Reuse NovaClient for credentials and async client lifetime
suggestions.rationale: `BedrockConverseBase` already resolves `AWS_CREDENTIALS`, bearer tokens, regions, retries, loop-local aioboto3 clients, and cleanup. A standalone shim that rereads configuration and creates sessions can drift from those rules and leak clients. Compose a configured `NovaClient`, enter and close it with the example run, and let the shim use its live Bedrock Runtime client.

suggestions.title: Match the complete InkWall perception tail
suggestions.rationale: The real Stage-1 implementation does more than the three named calls: it creates pipeline-owned shape IDs, maps anchors to slots, enables gap and bottom-row synthesis, optionally reads OCR, and assigns membership. Omitting that tail produces a `PerceptionResult` that is not equivalent to production and can break target selection or reconciliation. Reuse that exact behavior or test the example's generated perception against it.

suggestions.title: Keep OpenCV and file I/O off the event loop
suggestions.rationale: The pipeline routes perception, OCR, and rendering through its CPU executor. The example must apply the same rule to image decode, annotation, PNG/JPEG encoding, JSON reads, and output writes; direct `cv2.imread`/`imwrite` and synchronous path operations inside the main coroutine violate the async-first constraint.

suggestions.title: Define the flattening join and bbox convention explicitly
suggestions.rationale: `Identification` contains only an ID, while `IdentificationResult` does not carry boxes. The flat output must join slot IDs to `PerceptionResult.slots`, shape IDs to `PerceptionResult.shapes`, and added IDs to validated added `Shape` objects. Emit only pipeline-owned source-pixel boxes, such as `[x1,y1,x2,y2]`; do not expose Nova's normalized coordinates as the primary result bbox.

suggestions.title: Validate --boxes against the decoded image
suggestions.rationale: `from_strip_norm` relies on `PerceptionResult.image_size`, and annotation relies on actual array dimensions. Pydantic validation alone does not ensure that an override's image ID, dimensions, slot/anchor references, and every box match the supplied image. Fail fast on dimension mismatch and out-of-bounds boxes, with tests for stale and malformed overrides.

suggestions.title: Make the real retry and cost envelope visible
suggestions.rationale: There are two independent repair paths: `VisionAdapter` retries schema-invalid output, and `identify.py` retries a valid but incomplete response missing IDs. A strip can therefore consume three provider calls, which matters for the stated cost objective. Preserve the existing behavior if required, but record attempt counts and test the maximum explicitly.

suggestions.title: Test the exact Converse payload without AWS
suggestions.rationale: The highest-risk code is the transport boundary, not the pipeline reuse. A fake aioboto3 client should assert the model ID, image content block format and bytes, prompt/system schema instruction, temperature, token limit, response-text extraction, provider errors, and async close behavior. This catches a silently text-only request before any live experiment.

suggestions.title: Canonicalize the resolved Nova model before caching
suggestions.rationale: The repository maps `nova-2-lite` to `amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0`, while `NovaClient` applies the `us.` profile. `VisionAdapter.cache_key` uses the backend string, so alias-based and region-profile-based configurations can identify the same cache entry despite different effective routes. Pass the fully resolved model ID, including the profile prefix, into the shim and cache identity.

suggestions.title: Make ignored example files reliably trackable
suggestions.rationale: The broad `examples/planogram/*` rule still ignores a new `aws/` directory; existing negations cover only selected example subtrees. A one-time `git add -f` works for the initial files but future helpers or tests can disappear from commits. Add explicit negations and an ignore regression test, or enforce the force-add requirement in the contribution workflow.
